title: Frontend: Implement a Queue using Stack
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Implement a Queue using Stack. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(commands). Use two stacks for FIFO enqueue{value}, dequeue, peek, size. enqueue returns size; empty dequeue/peek return null. Transfer input to output only when output is empty.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Push new values onto an incoming stack.
alternativeApproaches: Explain amortized analysis using a potential function and contrast it with worst-case per-operation latency.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Interleaved operations; transfer boundary; empty queue.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
